mechanism: On each new D1 bar after 00:05, take prior daily OHLC. If close>open draw green Fib low→high; if close<open draw red Fib high→low. Levels: price = high-(high-low)*pct/100 (bull) or low+(high-low)*pct/100 (bear) at 23.6/38.2/50/61.8/100. Optional user fibRetracLvl (default 38.2) as buy (bull Fib) or sell (bear Fib) entry price. Second approach: over last N=100 bars on current TF, ArrayMaximum/Minimum of highs/lows; bull if open[100]<close[1] else bear; same Fib levels from array extrema.
data_needed: D1 open/high/low/close/time (shift 1) or CopyHigh/CopyLow/CopyRates of N bars; ObjectCreate OBJ_FIBO; NormalizeDouble levels.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol; Fib from PERIOD_D1 last candle; signals shown on M15; alternate N=100 bars on _Period.
why_new_for_mis: Automated daily (or N-bar) Fib grid oriented by candle/array direction gives MIS structural support/resistance and retracement-entry levels without manual drawing.
quote: if the last daily candle is bullish we need to get bullish FIBO from the low to high of the candle and price levels of each level

mechanism: Tick-wise geometric detectors on last 1–3 bars (PERIOD_CURRENT): Doji if open==close (buyer/seller balance). Hammer if body near top and lower shadow > longShadowRatio*range (default 0.7) with upper < smallShadowRatio*range (0.07); inverted hammer swaps shadows. Engulfing: last candle fully covers prior (high>high2, low<low2, close past prior open). Piercing/Dark Cloud: gap open then close beyond midpoint of prior body. Morning/Evening Star: small middle candle (size2 < 0.5*outer sizes) between opposite-colored longs. Three Inside Up/Down: middle bar inside first, third closes beyond first’s extreme.
data_needed: iOpen/iHigh/iLow/iClose/iTime shifts 1–3; candleSize=high-low; candleMidPoint2; ratio params.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol, PERIOD_CURRENT (any TF; author notes higher TF more significant).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit multi-bar OHLC geometry library (balance, rejection, engulf, midpoint reclaim, star, inside) as discrete change/reversal event sensors for MIS.
quote: This Doji candle indicates that there is a balance between buyers and sellers and no one controls the market

mechanism: Treat fixed-length equity increments dE as a random variable. Transform distributions to a relative scale so all have the same mean, then compare relative standard deviation σ*/μ*. Merging independent profitable curves (more instruments, longer horizon, or more parallel systems) strictly reduces that relative SD — the merged profit path is 'more beautiful' (straighter). Also: as test length → ∞, recovery factor → ∞ and relative equity DD → 0 iff the system is truly profitable; check RF↑ and relDD↓ across successively longer segments (or more symbols) as a profitability confirmation sensor.
data_needed: Equity/profit time series; segment length dT; per-segment Δequity; mean and stdev (or density law); recovery factor = TotalProfit/MaxEquityDD; relative DD.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic multi-instrument rebuy/averaging systems; parallel symbols on fixed test segment; no single named pair.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a distribution-theoretic stability sensor for strategy/portfolio equity paths and a horizon/instrument-count confirmation test for true edge vs random.
quote: The system having the smallest parameter is "the most beautiful"

mechanism: Brute-force EA groups are clustered by day-of-week and intraday time windows so each setting/copy only trades (and is scored) inside its cluster. Different clusters become independent robot groups; after live/demo filtering, groups split into direct-signal profitable (pattern inertia), inverted-signal profitable (immediate pattern change), or chaotic (fit). Prefer bar-based EAs with invert flag; maximize independent groups × (direct+inverted+mixed) signals.
data_needed: Generated EA settings; day-of-week and time-of-day filters; forward demo/real equity per group; invert-trade flag.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-symbol quote collector with configurable instrument/period lists; bar-by-bar MT4/MT5; years of history (YearsE).
why_new_for_mis: Calendar/time-window clustering of pattern applicability is a regime partition for when a statistical edge is live — usable as a MIS time-regime gate.
quote: clustering is represented by the possibility of dividing subgroups of robots by day of the week and time windows within a day

mechanism: For each EA group, run both the native signal and its full invert (buy↔sell). After a holdout period, retain groups that stay profitable on the direct path (inertia of the found pattern) or on the inverted path (pattern flipped / mean-reverted). Mixed cross-group signals add diversity. DaysToFuture kills stale settings; MinutesAwaitE polls shared-folder setting files.
data_needed: Universal receiver EA reading shared-folder setting files; bBruteforceInvertTrade; forward PnL for direct and inverted streams.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbols the quote-collector feeds; bar paradigm; demo/real signals over ~2 months in article.
why_new_for_mis: Treats pattern persistence vs flip as an explicit change sensor: keep both polarities and let live filtering decide inertia vs reversal regime.
quote: Profitable ones with a direct signal (based on the pattern inertia). Profitable with an inverted signal (based on an immediate pattern change).

mechanism: Custom ATR over PeriodATR bars but scaled to percent of mean OHLC: ATR% = 100 * (sumTrueRange/PeriodATR) / (sumPrice/(PeriodATR*4)), where sumPrice sums High+Low+Close+Open over the window and trueRange=high-low per bar. Relative ATR lets one weight work across many FX pairs without per-symbol recalibration; used with EMA distance gate (close-EMA < ATR*(1/K)) and RSI border for entries.
data_needed: OHLC arrays for PeriodATR bars; sumTrueRange; sumPrice; optional EMA, RSI, Bollinger for predicates.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-currency 28 FX pairs; H4 optimization 2018–2023 with 2023H1 forward.
why_new_for_mis: Percent-of-price ATR is a cross-asset volatility sensor that normalizes range across symbols for multi-currency MIS.

mechanism: getNextMove/getmove locate swing highs/lows: a bar is a swing if it is iHighest/iLowest over a window of count*2+1 centered near it (default checkBars=5). Take two successive highs and two lows. Regime: low1>low2 AND high1>high2 → Uptrend (HH+HL); high1<high2 AND low1<low2 → Downtrend (LH+LL); else Sideways. Draw ray trendlines through the two highs (red) and two lows (green).
data_needed: iHighest/iLowest on MODE_HIGH/MODE_LOW; iHigh/iLow/iTime; checkBars window.
why_new_for_mis: Structural swing-pair comparator yields a three-state trend regime (up/down/sideways) directly from price extrema — core MIS regime sensor.

mechanism: Using same two-swing highs/lows: Potential Double Top if high1≤high2 and low1>low2 (equal/lower high with higher trough); confirmed Double Top if high1≤high2 and low1<low2 (break of intervening low). Symmetric Double Bottom: potential if low1≥low2 and high1<high2; confirmed if low1≥low2 and high1>high2 (break of intervening high).
data_needed: Two swing high values and two swing low values from getmove; NormalizeDouble.
why_new_for_mis: Splits classic DT/DB into potential vs confirmed states via swing geometry — a staged reversal/change sensor for MIS.
quote: if the current high is lower than or equal to the previous one and at the same time the current low is lower than the previous one, this will be a signal of Double Top

mechanism: Recursively smoothed candles: haOpen=(haOpen_prev+haClose_prev)/2; haClose=(O+H+L+C)/4; haHigh=max(H,haOpen,haClose); haLow=min(L,haOpen,haClose). Color bullish (blue) if haOpen<haClose else bearish (red). Filters noise vs raw Japanese candles. Optional filter: buy if prior haClose > prior fast MA and fast MA > slow MA; sell if prior haClose < prior fast MA and fast MA < slow MA (periods 9/18).
data_needed: OHLC series; haOpen/High/Low/Close/Color buffers; optional iMA handles.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; HA in separate window; EMA/SMA periods 9 and 18 in combo EA.
why_new_for_mis: Heiken Ashi recursive smoothing is a noise-reduced directional regime sensor distinct from raw candle color.
quote: the aim of this indicator as per its calculation is to filter and eliminate some of the noise in the market movement by smoothing data

mechanism: Article derives lot sizing under linear, exponential (Kelly-like), and hyperbolic deposit-growth models from trade history, SL/TP, and risk R. No market regime/volatility/liquidity sensor is built — only position sizing given an already-positive expectancy strategy.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 2021–2022 test bed for MM comparison only.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: capital-growth / lot formulas only; no market sensing idea for MIS.
quote: money management is a set of rules that allows traders to calculate the optimal volume of positions

mechanism: True Strength Index: momentum m=close[i]-close[i+1]; abs m=|m|; double EMA smooth (default 25 then 13) on both; TSI=100*momSm2/absMomSm2. Oscillates about 0: TSI>0 bullish momentum, TSI<0 bearish; usable for OB/OS and divergence. Strategy gate: bullish SMA(10)/SMA(20) crossover and TSI>0 → buy; bearish crossover and TSI<0 → sell.
data_needed: Close series; ExponentialMAOnBuffer twice on mom and absMom; TSI buffer; optional iMA 10/20.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; smooth periods 25,13; MA 10/20 in system EA.
why_new_for_mis: Double-smoothed price-change / abs-change ratio is a low-noise momentum regime sensor around zero for MIS.
quote: Calculate TSI = 100*( Double-smoothed momentum / Double-smoothed absolute momentum)

mechanism: Donchian: CH=highest high of last N bars, CL=lowest low of last N, ML=(CH+CL)/2 (default N=20, plot shifted +1). Breakout regime: Ask>CH → buy (bullish power); Bid<CL → sell. Optional filter: Ask>CH and Ask>EMA(200) for buy; Bid<CL and Bid<EMA(200) for sell. Channel extremes also used as SL/TP anchors.
data_needed: high/low arrays; ArrayMaximum/ArrayMinimum over indPeriod; iCustom Donchian buffers; optional iMA EMA 200; Ask/Bid.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/PERIOD_CURRENT; period 20 default; EMA 200 filter variant.
why_new_for_mis: N-bar extrema channel with breakout-above/below states is a classic trend-following regime sensor; middle line adds equilibrium reference.
quote: If the price is above the highest high of a specific time, this indicates that there is a bullish power and this may be a buy signal

mechanism: Channel width = CH−CL over the Donchian lookback is the realized high–low range of the last N bars (distinct from Bollinger’s mean±σ). Width expansion/contraction tracks range volatility; author contrasts Donchian (raw extrema) with Bollinger (average ± two stdevs).
data_needed: Donchian upper and lower buffers; width=upper-lower per bar.
why_new_for_mis: N-period true range envelope (not stdev bands) gives MIS a simple range-volatility sensor from the same Donchian object used for breakouts.
quote: the Donchian Channels plot the highest high and the lowest low during a specific period of time ... but the Bollinger Bands plot an average of a period of time after adding and subtracting two standard deviations

mechanism: Part I teaches OnChartEvent CHARTEVENT_MOUSE_MOVE drag of an OBJ_RECTANGLE_LABEL dashboard (hit-test, MLB state, XDistance/YDistance update). Pure UI interactivity; no market sensing.
